answer: Agents must lock a bond before submitting work, and independent reviewers release it only after checking the result. One operator can create many identities, but each identity ties up real capital; splitting a yarrow report among accounts at a vertex does not create more value. If those accounts approve one another, a challenge can expose the collusion and slash their bonds. The attacker pays in locked funds and review effort, with costs rising for every fake identity spread across the canyon.
